title: Cytoskeleton Staining Protocol for RPMI 8226 by Immunofluorescence
author: Osei-Amponsa, Magidson, et al.
materials:
Timing: 30 min
2.Prepare fixation reagents.
Fixation reagent for 20 mL cell suspensionReagentsFinal concentrationVolume37% Formaldehyde (FA)4% after addition to cells2.457 mL10× Phosphate-Buffered Saline (PBS)1× in fixation reagent0.273 mLTOTALN/A2.73 mL
CRITICAL: Formaldehyde is toxic, handle in a fume hood.

steps.title: Culture RPMI 8226 cells
steps.instruction: Grow semi‑adherent RPMI 8226 cells in 20 mL appropriate medium (e.g., RPMI + 10 % FBS) in a T75 flask until ~80 % confluency (2–4 days). Ensure enough cells are generated to compensate for loss during preparation.

steps.title: Prepare fixation reagent
steps.instruction: Mix 2.457 mL of 37 % formaldehyde with 0.273 mL of 10× PBS (to give 4 % FA and 1× PBS final) to obtain 2.73 mL fixation reagent for 20 mL cell suspension. Handle formaldehyde in a fume hood (toxic).

steps.title: Prepare permeabilization‑quenching buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 32 mL of 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1.6 mL of 10 % Triton X‑100 (to give 1 % v/v), and 126.4 mL Milli‑Q water to make 160 mL buffer (final 200 mM Tris, 1 % Triton). Prepare fresh; can be stored at 4 °C if needed.

steps.title: Optional annexin V staining
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm orbital shaker to 37 °C. Add 10 µg Annexin V conjugate to the 20 mL culture medium in the T75 flask (per manufacturer’s protocol). Incubate at 37 °C, 100 rpm, 20 min in dim light, covering flask with aluminum foil.

substeps.instruction: Collect media with floating cells into a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 200 g, 10 min (Avanti J‑E, rotor JS‑5.3).
Rinse adherent cells in the flask with 5 mL 1× PBS (keep them moist).
Check under a light microscope that adherent cells remain.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 mL fresh RPMI (with or without supplement) and return to the original T75 flask after removing the PBS.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Add ~2.73 mL fixation reagent to the 20 mL cell suspension. Incubate at 37 °C, 100 rpm, 15 min in an orbital shaker. Gently detach cells by tapping the flask vertically for ≥1 min and pipetting up/down before adding fixative.

steps.title: Permeabilize and quench
steps.instruction: For each T75 flask, prepare four 50 mL conical tubes, add 40 mL permeabilization buffer to each (room temperature). Distribute the fixed cells equally (~5.7 mL per tube). Incubate on a rocking platform (VWR Model 100, setting 2) at 20–23 °C for 15 min to quench aldehydes.

steps.title: Centrifuge and DAPI stain
steps.instruction: Spin the four tubes at 200 g, 4 °C, 10 min. Aspirate supernatant leaving 2–3 mL, resuspend each pellet in its remaining supernatant, then combine all into a single 15 mL tube (~10 mL total). Count cells, add DAPI to a final 5 µg/mL. Incubate 20–23 °C, rocking at 2 rpm, 30 min. Centrifuge again at 200 g, 4 °C, 10 min, remove supernatant, and resuspend cells in 1× PBS to 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL. Cells may be stored at 4 °C with 0.02 % sodium azide for a few days.

steps.title: Incubate with fluorescent probes
steps.instruction: Transfer 0.2 mL of the cell suspension (~200 000 cells) to a 0.5 mL Eppendorf tube. Add ATTO‑643 phalloidin (final 100 nM; 1:100 dilution of 10 µM stock) and primary TUBB4A antibody (final 10 µg/mL; 1:30 dilution of 300 µg/mL stock). Cover with aluminum foil and incubate horizontally ~15 h on a rocking platform (VWR Model 100, setting 2) at 4 °C (alternatively 1–2 h at 37 °C, 100 rpm). Perform all steps in dim light.

steps.title: Attach cells to cover glass
steps.instruction: Place a 25 mm cover glass (labeled side up) at the bottom of a flat‑bottom 50 mL tube. Fill the tube with 50 mL 1× PBS. Transfer the entire 0.2 mL stained cell suspension into the tube. Centrifuge at 200 g, 4 °C, 10 min, handling gently to avoid detachment. Store at 4 °C up to 2 days (up to 3 weeks if 0.02 % sodium azide is added). Ensure the coated side of the glass remains facing up; otherwise, cap and gently rotate the tube to correct orientation. Note: residual conjugated antibodies may bind poly‑lysine on the glass, increasing background in wide‑field imaging but not in confocal microscopy.
